jurisdiction.name: France
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: France has no single AI law: it has not yet designated its EU AI Act authorities by law (the bill is before the Assemblée nationale), and the government has published only its planned scheme of competent authorities. AI is governed through sectoral provisions: deepfake offences in the 2024 SREN law, the algorithmic video-surveillance experiment created for the 2024 Olympics and extended to 2030, transparency rights for public-sector algorithmic decisions since 2016, AI duties in medicine, and decrees creating the Council for AI and Digital Affairs, the defence AI agency AMIAD and the PEReN expertise centre. National policy runs through a three-phase AI strategy since 2018, the 2024 AI Commission report and the 2025 'Osez l'IA' plan, while the State's June 2026 strategy for AI in public services, the common guide for public agents and ministry charters and strategies (Interior, Culture, Social Affairs, Health, Education, Armed Forces, Justice) govern AI use in government. Regulators are active: the CNIL's AI recommendations and its Clearview AI sanction, ANSSI security guidance, HAS guidance on AI in health, ACPR and AMF papers on AI in finance, and Competition Authority opinions on generative AI.
lead_institutions: Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés (CNIL)
Agence nationale de la sécurité des systèmes d'information (ANSSI)
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 11 October 2026 and covers national law, the national government and ministries, and regulators. Regional and city documents were not reviewed, in line with the project's rule for France. European Union and Council of Europe instruments are shown through the regional files. The bill naming France's AI Act authorities is still before parliament, so it is listed as a lead. Not yet verified from the official text: three documents, including the third phase of the national AI strategy.

instruments.summary: Official DGE page setting out the government's planned allocation of EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) supervision in France: the DGCCRF coordinates market surveillance authorities and acts as single point of contact; the CNIL supervises most Article 5 prohibited practices and most Annex III high-risk areas (biometrics, employment, law enforcement, migration, education with the DGCCRF, democratic processes with Arcom); Arcom and the DGCCRF supervise manipulative practices and Article 50 transparency/deepfake duties; the ACPR covers credit scoring and life/health insurance pricing; the Conseil d'État, Cour de cassation and Cour des comptes cover AI used by judicial authorities; defence and security senior officials cover critical infrastructure; existing Annex I product authorities (e.g. ANSM, ANFR, DGPR) keep their sectors. PEReN and ANSSI provide pooled technical expertise, and the DGE remains the strategic coordinator and France's representative on the European AI Board.

instruments.english_title: Building trust in AI through a cyber risk-based approach
instruments.current_status: Published by ANSSI on 7 February 2025 for the Paris AI Action Summit and co-signed in its English version by partner agencies (including BSI, NCSC-UK, CCCS, CSA Singapore, ACN and others); a French version ('Développer la confiance dans l'IA par une approche par les risques cyber') was published the same day.
instruments.summary: Joint high-level risk analysis, published by ANSSI and co-signed by around 20 international cyber agencies, on the cybersecurity of AI systems rather than AI-enabled security tools. It maps AI-related cyber risks across the AI supply chain (computing capacity, models and software libraries, data), including hosting-infrastructure compromise, supply-chain and data-integrity attacks and lateral movement through interconnected systems, building on the 2023 Guidelines for Secure AI System Development, and gives recommendations for users, operators and developers to assess threats and apply proportionate security measures.

instruments.summary: General digital-regulation law whose AI provisions target deepfakes. organizations.name: Parliament
organizations.ai_governance_role: French Parliament (Assemblée nationale and Sénat). Enacts laws with AI provisions: SREN deepfake offences (2024), the Olympic algorithmic video-surveillance experiment and its extensions (2023, 2026), algorithmic-decision transparency (2016), bioethics law AI-in-medicine duties (2021); the bill designating EU AI Act authorities was pending before it in October 2026.

organizations.name: Prime Minister
organizations.ai_governance_role: Head of government; chaired the interministerial AI committee of 6 February 2025; the Prime Minister's services (DSAF) issued their own charter on generative AI use; the AI Commission (2023-2024) was installed by the government and its report is published on the government site.

organizations.name: Directorate General for Enterprise
organizations.ai_governance_role: DGE (Ministry for the Economy): publishes and steers the economic side of the national AI strategy, the 'Osez l'IA' plan for AI adoption by businesses (July 2025) and practical AI guides for businesses.

organizations.name: Government of France
organizations.ai_governance_role: Central government of France. Adopts the national AI strategy (SNIA) and its phases under France 2030, steered by the national AI coordinator and the Secretariat-General for Investment, including the third phase launched at the interministerial AI committee of 6 February 2025.

organizations.name: French Artificial Intelligence Commission
organizations.ai_governance_role: Expert commission installed by the government in September 2023 (co-chaired by Anne Bouverot and Philippe Aghion); delivered the report 'IA : notre ambition pour la France' with 25 recommendations on 13 March 2024.

organizations.name: Interministerial Directorate for Digital Affairs
organizations.ai_governance_role: DINUM: runs the 'IA dans l'État' programme (interministerial AI platform, Albert API, L'Assistant, ALLiaNCE incubator, AI compliance unit, portal of AI charters, ministerial AI roadmaps) and co-authored the 2026 Guide d'usage de l'IA for State agents and the responsible AI procurement factsheet (MiNumEco).

organizations.name: State Purchasing Directorate
organizations.ai_governance_role: Direction des Achats de l'État (DAE): State purchasing directorate; co-author of the responsible AI procurement factsheet (November 2025).

organizations.name: Ministry of Higher Education and Research
organizations.ai_governance_role: Leads the research pillar of the national AI strategy (national AI research strategy, 28 November 2018; 3IA institutes, AI chairs, Jean Zay); hosts the second-phase press kit (8 November 2021).

organizations.name: Ministry of the Interior
organizations.ai_governance_role: Adopted a ministerial AI roadmap (6 May 2025) and a charter for ethical uses of AI distributed by circular in March 2026.

organizations.name: Ministry of Culture
organizations.ai_governance_role: Published its AI action strategy for cultural, responsible and sovereign AI (2 July 2025) and an internal charter for reasoned and responsible AI use (June 2026).

organizations.name: Social Affairs Ministries
organizations.ai_governance_role: Ministries for labour, health, solidarity and related portfolios sharing a Secretariat-General and Digital Directorate; issued a charter on AI use within the social ministries (December 2025).

organizations.name: Ministry of Health
organizations.ai_governance_role: Ministry of Health, Families, Autonomy and Persons with Disabilities; adopted the Stratégie intelligence artificielle et données de santé 2025-2028 (November 2025).

organizations.name: Ministry of National Education
organizations.ai_governance_role: Published the 'Cadre d'usage de l'IA en éducation' (June 2025) setting the framework for AI use in schools.

organizations.name: Ministry of the Armed Forces
organizations.ai_governance_role: Defence AI strategy since 2019 (Task Force IA report), ministerial AI strategy instruction of 18 January 2024, Agence ministérielle pour l'IA de défense (AMIAD, 2024); its Defence Ethics Committee issued an opinion on AI use by the armed forces (published February 2025).

organizations.name: Ministry of Justice
organizations.ai_governance_role: Published the working-group report 'L'IA au service de la justice : stratégie et solutions opérationnelles' (23 June 2025).

organizations.name: Council of State
organizations.ai_governance_role: Highest administrative court and government legal adviser; published the study 'Intelligence artificielle et action publique' at the Prime Minister's request (30 August 2022) and the charter on AI use within the administrative jurisdiction (December 2025).

organizations.name: Directorate General for Administration and the Civil Service
organizations.ai_governance_role: DGAFP: published the strategy for AI use in HR management in the State civil service (June 2024) and co-authored the 2026 Guide d'usage de l'IA for State agents.

organizations.name: French Data Protection Authority (CNIL)
organizations.ai_governance_role: Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés: independent administrative authority enforcing the GDPR and the Loi Informatique et Libertés; issues AI recommendations (fiches pratiques IA), positions on augmented cameras and generative AI, runs AI sandboxes and sanctions unlawful AI-related processing (e.g. Clearview AI, 2022).

organizations.name: National Cybersecurity Agency of France
organizations.ai_governance_role: Agence nationale de la sécurité des systèmes d'information (ANSSI), attached to the Secretary-General for National Defence and Security; publishes AI security guidance (generative AI security recommendations 2024, cyber risk-based approach to AI 2025) and joint publications with partner agencies.

organizations.name: Regulatory Authority for Audiovisual and Digital Communication
organizations.ai_governance_role: Autorité de régulation de la communication audiovisuelle et numérique (Arcom): independent media and online-platform regulator; publishes studies and positions on AI, generative AI and information integrity, and is designated Digital Services Coordinator.

organizations.name: Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority
organizations.ai_governance_role: Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution (ACPR), attached to the Banque de France: supervises banks and insurers; publishes discussion papers and supervisory positions on AI governance and model risk in finance.

organizations.name: Financial Markets Authority
organizations.ai_governance_role: Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF): financial markets regulator; publishes studies and positions on AI use by market participants and asset managers.

organizations.name: French National Authority for Health
organizations.ai_governance_role: Haute Autorité de santé (HAS): independent public scientific authority for health; publishes guidance on the evaluation of AI-based medical devices and on the use of AI (including generative AI) by health and social-care professionals.

organizations.name: French Competition Authority
organizations.ai_governance_role: Autorité de la concurrence: independent competition regulator; issued opinions on competition in generative AI (2024) and related AI markets.

organizations.name: Defender of Rights
organizations.ai_governance_role: Défenseur des droits: constitutional independent authority for rights and anti-discrimination; publishes reports and opinions on algorithms, AI and discrimination in public services.

organizations.name: National Pilot Committee for Digital Ethics
organizations.ai_governance_role: Comité national pilote d'éthique du numérique (CNPEN), created in 2019 under the aegis of the CCNE: official advisory body that issues ethics opinions on digital technologies and AI, including generative AI (Opinion 7, 2023).

organizations.name: Evaluation Committee of the Algorithmic Video-Protection Experiment
organizations.ai_governance_role: Statutory evaluation committee set up under Article 10 of Law No. 2023-380 and Decree No. 2023-939; its January 2025 report evaluates the AI video-protection experiment.

organizations.name: Higher Council for Literary and Artistic Property (CSPLA)
organizations.ai_governance_role: Advisory body of the Ministry of Culture on literary and artistic property; its mission reports address remuneration for cultural content used by AI systems and other AI copyright issues.

organizations.name: National Consultative Ethics Committee (CCNE)
organizations.ai_governance_role: National Consultative Ethics Committee for Health and Life Sciences; adopted joint Opinion 141 with the CNPEN on medical diagnosis and AI (November 2022).

organizations.name: Ministry of Agriculture and Food Sovereignty
organizations.ai_governance_role: Ministry of Agriculture and Food Sovereignty; its Secretariat-General (SNUM) issued service note SG/SNUM/2025-364 introducing an AI charter for ministry staff.

organizations.name: Government Information Service (SIG)
organizations.ai_governance_role: Service d'information du Gouvernement (Prime Minister): issued the charter for the responsible use of AI by State communicators (February 2026).

organizations.name: Regulatory Authority for Electronic Communications, Postal Services and Press Distribution (Arcep)
organizations.ai_governance_role: Telecoms and digital-infrastructure regulator; publishes work on the environmental footprint of digital services, including its May 2026 report on generative AI.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: National law, the government and its ministries (including the State digital directorate's doctrine and the Council of State), and regulators and independent authorities were searched at national level in a review on 2026-10-11, with EU and Council of Europe documents listed in the regional pages. No qualifying AI-governance document was found for standards. Several ministry sites (economy, higher education, education, digital health, agriculture) were unavailable, three documents are listed without a full check of their text, and the pending DDADUE bill is listed under Leads to check later.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: Backfill run 2026-10-11 in three parts (F1 law via Légifrance; F2 government incl. ministry-level search, DINUM doctrine and Conseil d'État; F3 regulators and independent authorities), national level only per PROTOCOL §6. Run in parallel with ESP on separate branches. No interruption. All six earlier records re-checked and fixed: AI Act authorities page dated 2025-09-09 and recorded as the DGE's planned scheme (no designation act yet; DDADUE bill pending at the Assemblée nationale, held as lead); France 2030 record re-pointed to the 2021 second-phase strategy and marked superseded by phase 3; procurement fiche re-sourced to its PDF; charter portal replaced by the June 2026 Guide d'usage de l'IA; ANSSI and CNIL records retitled and dated. Stale domain-named sources/organisations dropped. EU and CoE instruments are attached via the regional files. Access: legifrance.gouv.fr 403 to curl (all texts read via WebFetch); info.gouv.fr and economie.gouv.fr HTML 403 to both methods; enseignementsup-recherche.gouv.fr, education.gouv.fr, esante.gouv.fr, info.agriculture.gouv.fr blocked; guides.etalab.gouv.fr DNS failure; acpr.banque-france.fr 403 to curl (WebFetch worked); defenseurdesdroits.fr reset to curl. Located-only (3): SNIA phase 3 (2025-02-06), Villani report (2018-03-28), Cadre d'usage de l'IA en éducation (2025-06). Ministry charters hosted on DINUM's ia.numerique.gouv.fr (State portal); Armed Forces 2019 report and ethics opinion read on vie-publique.fr (DILA, State publisher). Autorité de la concurrence 24-A-05 read from the official English translation (French PDF 54.7 MB not downloaded). standards: no material found.
Wording note 2026-10-19 (narrative.review_notes): Three documents, including the third phase of the national AI strategy, could only be located because the government websites blocked access to them.
Catch-up sweep 2026-10-19: checked Senate and Assemblée nationale dossiers of the DDADUE bill (Sénat n° 118 / AN n° 2518; still at first reading in the Assemblée, no adoption, CMP or promulgation, so no national AI Act designation law yet; lead unchanged), CNIL news (to 16 Oct 2026; no new AI item; the 16 Oct CNIL/ICO/CNPD finance study is not AI-specific), DGE AI pages (14 Oct 2026 call for expressions of interest for legal-sector AI solutions is a funding call, out of scope), ANSSI publications list, Légifrance (discovery search, no AI text dated October 2026). Found nothing new. Not reached: ACPR publications (403), HAS publications (403).
